lockedMove.speaker: Richard Dawkins
lockedMove.proposition: A moving personal recovery does not by itself establish Christianity, because identifying as Christian entails definite supernatural claims about Jesus that require belief.
lockedMove.sourceExcerpt: moving personal story. But to call yourself a Christian is a bit different. I mean, a Christian has to believe in something. You go to church now. And you listen to the vicar. Do you notice what a lot of nonsense he talks about? I mean, do you really take it seriously that Jesus is the Son of God? That Jesus rose from the dead? Jesus was born of a virgin? That is a part of Christianity

components.text: Whether the reported recovery rationally identifies Christianity rather than merely recording a powerful personal experience.
Whether the experience supplies support for Christianity's definite claims about Jesus.

response.rationale: Dawkins expressly separates the moving recovery story from the further requirements of Christian identity, names concrete doctrines, and states the defeating consequence that recovery alone does not establish them.
